title: Ezekiel Bible Quiz - Chapter 24
description: Ten questions on Ezekiel 24: the parable of the cauldron, the day Babylon's king drew close to Jerusalem, and the sign the prophet had to be for the people.

questions.text: According to this chapter, who drew close to Jerusalem on the day the prophet had to write down?
questions.explanation: The word came in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day, and that same day the king of Babylon drew close to Jerusalem.

questions.text: What was to be put on the fire in the parable told to the rebellious house?
questions.explanation: The parable says: put the cauldron on the fire, put it on, and also pour water into it.

questions.text: What was to be placed under the cauldron?
questions.explanation: The parable says to take the choice of the flock, and also a pile of wood for the bones under the cauldron.

questions.text: What does this chapter call the city in its woe?
questions.explanation: The Lord Yahweh says: woe to the bloody city, to the cauldron whose rust is in it.

questions.text: Where does the chapter say the city set her blood?
questions.explanation: It says her blood is in the middle of her; she set it on the bare rock and did not pour it on the ground to cover it with dust.

questions.text: Why does the chapter say the city will not be cleansed any more?
questions.explanation: It says that because he had cleansed her and she was not cleansed, she will not be cleansed from her filthiness any more until his wrath has rested.

answers.text: Because her priests had fled to the mountains
Because her walls were broken down by strangers
Because her wells had dried up in the drought
Because he had cleansed her and she was not cleansed

questions.text: What was the prophet told about the desire of his eyes?
questions.explanation: He was told that the desire of his eyes would be taken away with a stroke, yet he should neither mourn nor weep, and his tears should not run down.

answers.text: It would be taken away with a stroke
It would be given back to him
It would be carried to Babylon
It would be hidden in the sanctuary

questions.text: What happened at evening on the day he spoke to the people?
questions.explanation: He spoke to the people in the morning, and at evening his wife died; and in the morning he did as he was commanded.

questions.text: What were the people told they would not do when the news came?
questions.explanation: They were told they would do as he had done: they would not cover their lips or eat mourner's bread, but would pine away in their iniquities.

answers.text: They would not pray or fast in the sanctuary
They would not cover their lips or eat mourner's bread
They would not leave their houses or shut the doors
They would not speak to one another in the streets

questions.text: What does the chapter say Ezekiel will be to the people?
questions.explanation: It says that Ezekiel will be a sign to them, and that according to all he has done, they will do.
